The write is cargo extracting a dependency, not an agent-config implant.","reasoning":"Ancestry and captured /proc state account for the whole mechanism: systemd -> dockerd -> runc (--bundle /var/lib/docker/buildkit/executor/...) -> /bin/sh -c 'cargo chef cook --release -p nanosiem-lake-worker ...' -> cargo -> cargo-chef -> cargo build (pid 2764856, in-container NSpid 16, uid 0 inside the container, cwd /app). process.json shows a stock rust:1.98 image environment (CARGO_HOME=/usr/local/cargo, RUSTUP_HOME=/usr/local/rustup, RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.98.0, RUSTFLAGS mold link-arg) and fd 3 held on /usr/local/cargo/.package-cache — the lock cargo holds while it is downloading and extracting registry packages. The written path is $CARGO_HOME/registry/src/index.crates.io-<hash>/<crate>-<version>/, which is precisely the directory cargo extracts a downloaded .crate tarball into, so every file the tarball contains gets written there; a crate whose published sources include AGENTS.md trips this rule on first fetch by construction. That reading does not rest on the file's name or on any string the crate author chose: alerts.jsonl shows the same rule firing in the same build pass, seconds apart, for several unrelated well-known crates on different agent-config filenames (zerocopy-0.8.47/AGENTS.md, rend-0.4.2/.vscode/tasks.json, sharded-slab-0.1.7/.envrc, and earlier camino-1.2.2/.claude/settings.json and zerocopy-0.8.40/AGENTS.md from a prior cargo run) — a batch-extraction signature, not a targeted implant, and the accompanying persist-git-hook-write from the same pid is the same tarball-unpack behaviour. The 'pkg-install' context is moat's basename match on `cargo`, and /var/log/pacman.log records no transaction anywhere in the 13:50-14:10 window, so no system package install was involved; 'no package owns this path' is expected for a container-internal cargo cache. The rule's own message ('runs automatically on your next login') is false here — nothing reads a crate's AGENTS.md out of a throwaway build container's registry cache. Not verifiable, and the reason confidence is not lower: the target file could not be staged (meta.json copied: [], content 'No such file or directory') because it lives in the container's mount namespace and the layer is gone, so I could not inspect the AGENTS.md bytes; that limits what I can say about that crate's content, but not about the mechanism that wrote it, which is fully explained. The 'first_seen' rarity is expected for a first fetch of a specific crate version. Broader noise in the same window (exec-untrusted-home/tmpfs floods, cred reads, net-first-contact) belongs to other pids and other build/test tooling, not to this process.","proposed_allowlist":"# cargo extracts each downloaded .crate tarball into
